problem: Given the ellipsoid $(x-1)^{2}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(z-5)^{2}}{2}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$

feedback.problem: Given the sphere $(x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}+(z+3)^{2}=3,$ what is the domain of $z=z(x,y)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the equation of the sphere, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}+(z+3)^{2} & =3 \\ (z+3)^{2} & =3-((x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}) \\ z+3 & =\pm \sqrt{3-((x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2})} \\ z & =-3\pm \sqrt{3-((x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2})}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}3-((x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2})\ge 0 \\ (x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}\le 3\end{aligned}
$$

This inequality describes the interior and boundary of the circle 

$$
(x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=3
$$

which is a circle of radius $\sqrt{3}$ centered at $(-1,3)$ in the $xy$-plane.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: The interior and boundary of the circle of radius $\sqrt{3}$  centered at $(-1,3)$
